heuristics.rule: Assess trust rebuilding by observable behaviors, not reported feelings
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a partner is genuinely rebuilding trust after infidelity...
heuristics.action: ...check for three concrete behaviors: cessation of affair partner contact, voluntary transparency about whereabouts, and proactive disclosure of any accidental contact — before weighing emotional claims
heuristics.because: Feelings of readiness to trust are unfalsifiable in the moment; these behaviors are independently checkable and function as leading indicators of actual trustworthiness

heuristics.rule: Treat a setback during trust rebuilding as expected process, not evidence of failure
heuristics.condition: When a regression or painful episode occurs during the trust-rebuilding period after infidelity...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate whether the behavioral commitments (no contact, transparency, proactive disclosure) remain intact rather than treating the emotional setback as proof the process has broken down
heuristics.because: Research explicitly identifies the process as non-linear; mistaking a predictable setback for process failure causes premature exit from a potentially repairable situation

heuristics.rule: Distinguish punitive surveillance from trust-building accountability
heuristics.condition: When the betrayed partner is considering or requesting concrete monitoring measures (shared location, access to messages)...
heuristics.action: ...frame and implement these as time-limited trust-building mechanisms initiated by the involved partner, not as ongoing punishment
heuristics.because: The research distinguishes accountability measures as trust signals when voluntarily offered; when experienced as punitive, they undermine rather than build the emotional safety needed for repair

heuristics.rule: Require proactive disclosure of accidental contact as a binary test
heuristics.condition: When the affair partner is part of the same social, professional, or geographic environment and complete avoidance is impractical...
heuristics.action: ...treat whether the involved partner volunteers accidental contact disclosures unprompted as a hard diagnostic — this is a higher-signal behavior than the absence of deliberate contact
heuristics.because: Proactive disclosure in low-stakes accidental moments is a strong behavioral indicator of sustained commitment to transparency rather than compliance under surveillance

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Without this, all other trust-rebuilding behaviors are undermined; it is the threshold condition for repair to be possible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly whether contact has stopped; ask what specific boundaries have been put in place to prevent accidental contact; verify consistency between stated steps and observable circumstances

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Transparency offered only when asked indicates strategic information management; voluntary transparency indicates internalized commitment to repair
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe whether the involved partner initiates disclosures or waits to be questioned; note whether accountability measures (location sharing, phone access) were offered or extracted

decision_factors.why_it_matters: This is a high-signal behavior because it occurs in moments when concealment would likely go undetected; its presence or absence distinguishes genuine commitment from performance
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the involved partner ever come forward about an accidental encounter before being asked? If accidental contact is implausible in their circumstances, has any similar low-stakes honesty test been observable?

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Showing up to scheduled hard conversations with honesty and non-defensiveness is identified as a distinct trust-building behavior; defensiveness during repair conversations signals prioritization of self-protection over the relationship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Observe the involved partner's behavior specifically in planned difficult conversations, not casual ones; defensiveness is easier to suppress in low-stakes moments

decision_factors.factor: Bilateral effort in the rebuilding process
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Research identifies trust rebuilding as requiring conscious sustained effort from BOTH partners; a process borne entirely by one partner is not the process the evidence describes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether the betrayed partner is also engaging actively (e.g., attending therapy, naming what they need, working on reactivity) versus the full burden sitting with the involved partner or vice versa

decision_factors.factor: Consistency over calendar time versus calendar time alone
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The literature explicitly rejects a fixed timeline; trust is a function of behavioral consistency, meaning six months of inconsistent behavior is weaker evidence than three months of consistent behavior
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track behavioral consistency across the observable indicators rather than counting months; note whether any deviations were proactively disclosed or discovered

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Staying and attempting trust rebuilding after infidelity
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The non-linear nature of the process means the betrayed partner will experience re-traumatization during setbacks even when the process is working; choosing to stay does not mean choosing to stop being hurt in the near term
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Betrayed partners who interpret ongoing pain as evidence the decision to stay was wrong, leading to repeated re-evaluation rather than committed process engagement

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on monitored communication and location sharing as the primary trust-rebuilding mechanism
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Surveillance-dependent trust creates a relationship structure that requires permanent monitoring to feel secure; it does not build the internalized trust that can eventually remove the monitoring
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Couples who treat accountability tools as end-states rather than transitional scaffolding

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting verbal assurances of no contact without behavioral evidence
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Verbal assurances are unfalsifiable until a contradiction surfaces; building a repair process on them means the foundation of the process is invisible and the betrayed partner cannot distinguish genuine repair from a more sophisticated concealment
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Betrayed partners who are conflict-averse or who want to believe the repair is working and therefore avoid pressing for observable evidence

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Treating trust rebuilding as a bilateral process requiring active effort from both partners
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: This places a genuine processing and behavioral burden on the betrayed partner, who is already the injured party; the research framing is clinically accurate but can be experienced as unfair by the person who did not cause the rupture
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Betrayed partners in individual therapy who are told they must also 'do the work,' which can feel like being asked to repair damage they did not cause

failure_patterns.pattern: Using the feeling of trust as the primary metric for repair progress
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Trust is experienced as an emotion, so it feels natural to use emotional readiness as the measure; the observable behavioral indicators require deliberate external tracking and feel less intuitive
failure_patterns.consequence: The betrayed partner has no way to distinguish a genuine trust signal from wishful thinking or fatigue-driven resignation; decisions about whether to stay or leave are made on unfalsifiable grounds
warning_signs: Partner says 'I just feel like things are better now' without being able to point to specific behavioral changes
Evaluation of progress resets entirely after each painful episode rather than returning to a behavioral baseline

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating a non-linear setback as evidence the process has failed and the relationship is irreparable
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Setbacks are emotionally indistinguishable from the original betrayal in the moment; without an explicit framework that normalizes non-linearity, each painful episode reads as a new data point rather than expected variation
failure_patterns.consequence: Premature exit from a repairable relationship, or alternatively, repeated near-exits that destabilize the process and make genuine repair harder
warning_signs: Every difficult conversation or emotional regression triggers a full re-evaluation of whether to leave
Partner frames setbacks as 'we're back to square one' rather than as expected turbulence within a process

failure_patterns.pattern: Confusing monitoring compliance with trust rebuilding
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Shared phone access and location tracking are visible and concrete, making them feel like evidence of trustworthiness; the actual trust-building behaviors (proactive disclosure, non-defensive honesty) are more effort-intensive and less legible
failure_patterns.consequence: The couple structures repair around surveillance rather than internalized commitment; trust does not generalize beyond the monitored contexts
warning_signs: The involved partner is transparent only in contexts where monitoring is active
The betrayed partner's sense of security collapses entirely during any gap in monitoring rather than persisting

failure_patterns.pattern: Requiring the involved partner to demonstrate remorse emotionally rather than behaviorally
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Emotional remorse is immediately satisfying and visible; behavioral consistency is slow and accumulates over time, making it feel less like repair in the short term
failure_patterns.consequence: The process centers on performances of guilt rather than the actual behavioral indicators the research identifies as trust-building; the involved partner may become skilled at emotional expression without the underlying behavioral change
warning_signs: The betrayed partner reports feeling reassured after intense emotional conversations but uncertain again within days
Repair milestones are measured by how bad the involved partner appeared to feel rather than by what they did differently

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the involved partner stopped all contact with the affair partner, and what specific steps have been taken to prevent accidental contact?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the threshold condition for repair is present; the specificity of the answer distinguishes genuine structural change from vague intention
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have there been any accidental encounters since? If so, did your partner tell you before you asked?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is the stated reason contact has not stopped, and does the betrayed partner accept that reason as legitimate?

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the involved partner ever voluntarily disclosed something about their whereabouts or the affair partner without being asked?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether transparency is proactive or reactive; proactive disclosure in low-stakes moments is a stronger signal of internalized commitment than disclosure under direct questioning
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What did they disclose, and did it come before or after you had any reason to ask?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is all transparency in this relationship currently initiated by the betrayed partner's questions rather than the involved partner's offerings?

diagnostic_questions.question: When the two of you have a planned difficult conversation about the infidelity, how does the involved partner typically show up — defensive or non-defensive?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the involved partner is prioritizing self-protection or relationship repair in the moments that most directly test their commitment to the process
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does non-defensiveness persist throughout the conversation or appear early and then shift when the questions get specific?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What form does the defensiveness take — denial, minimization, counter-attack, or shutdown?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are both partners actively doing something to participate in the repair process, or is the work sitting almost entirely with one person?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the process matches the research model of bilateral effort; unilateral repair processes are structurally different from what the evidence describes and may be less likely to produce durable trust
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specifically is the betrayed partner doing, and is it experienced as active engagement or exhausting obligation?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Which partner is carrying the full burden, and what is the stated reason the other partner is not engaged?

diagnostic_questions.question: When a painful setback or regression occurs, how do both partners interpret it — as evidence the process has failed or as expected non-linearity?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the couple has a shared framework for the process that can absorb difficulty; couples without this framework are vulnerable to premature exit or recursive re-traumatization
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Has this framework been explicitly named between the partners or is it just a shared implicit tolerance?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Does every setback trigger a full re-evaluation of whether the relationship is over?

industry_realities.common_belief: Trust after infidelity rebuilds gradually on its own as time passes and the affair recedes into the past
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research identifies trust rebuilding as requiring conscious, sustained, active effort from both partners — time without effort does not produce the outcome; the mechanism is behavioral consistency, not elapsed calendar time
industry_realities.implication: Couples who are 'waiting it out' without a structured behavioral process are likely not rebuilding trust; the passage of time is neither necessary nor sufficient

industry_realities.common_belief: Progress in trust rebuilding should feel steady and cumulative — if it feels like you're going backward, something is wrong
industry_realities.actual_reality: The literature explicitly identifies the process as non-linear; setbacks are expected features of the process, not evidence it has broken down
industry_realities.implication: Evaluating the health of a repair process by whether it feels emotionally smooth will produce false negatives; the correct evaluation criterion is whether the behavioral commitments remain intact through the setbacks

industry_realities.common_belief: The primary indicator that trust is rebuilding is the betrayed partner's increasing emotional sense of security
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research points to observable behavioral indicators on the involved partner's side — cessation of contact, voluntary transparency, proactive disclosure of accidental contact, non-defensiveness in hard conversations — as the evidence base for repair, not the betrayed partner's emotional state alone
industry_realities.implication: Emotional security can be manufactured by avoidance, denial, or fatigue-driven acceptance; behavioral evidence is harder to fake and provides a more reliable diagnostic

industry_realities.common_belief: Monitoring tools like shared phone access are a sign the relationship is damaged and not truly repaired
industry_realities.actual_reality: The research treats concrete accountability measures as legitimate trust-building actions during the repair period, not as indicators of ongoing dysfunction — the COVID-19 period's constraints produced monitored communication as a natural accountability structure and this was studied as a positive feature
industry_realities.implication: Temporary structured accountability is a clinically recognized part of the repair process, not a sign of failure; the question is whether it remains time-limited and scaffolding rather than becoming permanent control

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How to evaluate whether trust is being rebuilt
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Asks the betrayed partner 'do you feel like you trust them more?' and uses the emotional answer as the primary data point
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Asks for specific behavioral evidence: has contact stopped, has there been proactive disclosure, what does non-defensiveness look like in their actual recent conversations — then triangulates the emotional report against the behavioral record
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Emotional trust assessments are unfalsifiable in the moment and susceptible to wishful thinking, fatigue, or coercion; behavioral evidence is independently checkable and distinguishes genuine repair from performance

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Interpreting setbacks during the repair process
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats each regression or painful episode as a new data point about whether the relationship is repairable, triggering a fresh cost-benefit analysis each time
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Holds the non-linear frame explicitly — evaluates whether the underlying behavioral commitments remain intact through the setback rather than treating the emotional pain of the setback as the signal
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Without the non-linear frame, every setback destabilizes the entire repair process and the couple never accumulates the consistent behavioral record that actually builds trust

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Sees monitoring as either a necessary permanent arrangement or a humiliating sign that the relationship hasn't truly healed
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Frames monitoring as time-limited transitional scaffolding that serves a specific trust-building function and should be designed to become unnecessary as behavioral consistency accumulates
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The framing determines whether accountability tools are implemented in ways that can eventually be removed versus ways that entrench surveillance as the structural basis of the relationship

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Assigning responsibility for the repair process
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Assigns repair responsibility primarily to the involved partner (they broke it, they fix it) or accepts whatever bilateral framing the couple presents without examining whether actual bilateral effort is occurring
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Uses the research finding that both partners must engage consciously to stress-test whether the process is genuinely bilateral — and distinguishes between the involved partner's behavioral obligations (which are primary) and the betrayed partner's active process engagement (which is also required for the model to work)
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A unilateral repair process may produce surface-level stability without the durable trust the research describes; identifying the actual distribution of effort reveals whether the process is structurally sound
